messages.subject: Question on Regression
parts:
I'm currently having trouble running a linear regression in R. The
degrees of freedom aren't what they should be. The following is the
output based off a 1000 sample size where y and x are vectors:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
> t<-lm(z$y~z$x)
> anova(t)
Analysis of Variance Table

Response: z$y
Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)
z$x 997 246788 248 85.65 0.01161 *
Residuals 2 6 3
---
Signif. codes: 0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
However, I'm only regressing one independent variable x on y. The z$x
degrees of freedom should equal 1 (k - 1 = 1), yet it is outputting
degrees of freedom of 997!!! Has anyone had this problem before and/
or are they aware of what I am doing wrong? Thanks ahead of time!

Guy123

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: Question on Regression
parts:
Like z$x is being treated as a factor, rather than as numeric as you
expect.

Try this:

y <- z$y
x <- as.numeric(as.character(z$x))

anova(lm(y~x))

karl
